claims.summary: For stress / anxiety, Fish Oil has moderate human evidence (26 studies).

explanation.what_it_is: Fish oil is a fat extracted from fatty fish (salmon, mackerel, sardines) that is rich in omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids, primarily EPA (eicosapentaenoic acid) and DHA (docosahexaenoic acid). These are essential fats your body cannot make on its own and must obtain from diet or supplements.
explanation.how_it_works: EPA and DHA integrate into cell membranes throughout your body, where they influence cell signaling, reduce production of inflammatory molecules, and support neurotransmitter function. In the brain, DHA is a major structural component that helps maintain neural connections and may stabilize serotonin and dopamine pathways. In the cardiovascular system, these fats help regulate blood vessel function, reduce triglycerides, and lower inflammatory markers that contribute to arterial damage. In the gut, omega-3s promote beneficial bacteria growth and strengthen the intestinal barrier.

proven_benefits.note: Substantial human evidence (28 studies) shows fish oil can support mood regulation and reduce depressive symptoms, likely through effects on brain serotonin and inflammation.
Well-supported by human research (28 studies) demonstrating measurable reductions in systemic inflammatory markers.
Consistent human evidence (22 studies) shows benefits for heart health markers including blood pressure, triglycerides, and arterial function.
Supported by human studies (29 studies) indicating improvements in gut barrier function and beneficial changes to bacterial composition.
Moderate human evidence (26 studies) suggests fish oil can help reduce anxiety and support stress resilience, though effects vary by individual.

explanation.emerging_research: Recent research is exploring whether omega-3s may support cognitive aging and whether specific EPA-to-DHA ratios optimize different outcomes (mood vs. cardiovascular). Some studies are investigating fish oil's role in autoimmune conditions and metabolic health, though these remain early-stage investigations.
explanation.caveats: Fish oil supplements vary widely in EPA/DHA content and purity; third-party testing is advisable. High doses may increase bleeding risk in those on anticoagulants, and some users report fish-flavored aftertaste or mild gastrointestinal upset. Quality sources and consistent dosing matter for reliable benefits.
